messages.subject: Rcpp dependency not installed - was "RE: [R] installing Packages"
parts:
This may be one for Hadley Wickham, the ggplot2 package maintainer.
It's not obvious from the CRAN listings for ggplot2 and Rcpp that there is a ggplot2 dependency on, or import from, Rcpp at all, and the listed reverse depends/imports for Rcpp don’t include any of the imports in ggplot2 either. Could that be why the default (NA) for dependencies is not picking up and installing Rcpp?

I've cc'd to the google group (I hope) to permit further discussion there.

S Ellison

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Rcpp dependency not installed - was "RE: [R] installing Packages"
parts:
On 1/27/15 5:03 AM, S Ellison wrote:
> This may be one for Hadley Wickham, the ggplot2 package maintainer.
> It's not obvious from the CRAN listings for ggplot2 and Rcpp that
> there is a ggplot2 dependency on, or import from, Rcpp at all, and
> the listed reverse depends/imports for Rcpp don’t include any of the
> imports in ggplot2 either.

There is at least an indirect relationship. Both plyr and reshape2,
which are imports of ggplot2, import from Rcpp.

> Could that be why the default (NA) for
> dependencies is not picking up and installing Rcpp?

I don't believe so. I just tried installing ggplot2 in an empty library
(with only the recommended packages available in the system library) and
I got

> install.packages("ggplot2")
Installing package into ‘/Users/schnade/Library/R/3.1/library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
also installing the dependencies ‘colorspace’, ‘Rcpp’, ‘stringr’,
‘RColorBrewer’, ‘dichromat’, ‘munsell’, ‘labeling’, ‘plyr’, ‘digest’,
‘gtable’, ‘reshape2’, ‘scales’, ‘proto’
[...rest of output not shown...]

> "Rcpp" %in% rownames(installed.packages())
[1] TRUE

So Rcpp would get installed with the default arguments.

> I've cc'd to the google group (I hope) to permit further discussion
> there.

My guess as to what happened (and this is based on it having happened to
me before with a different package) is that something failed in the Rcpp
installation (as simple as a network timeout) and that fact got buried
in the output which went scrolling by. Failing to install one of the
dependencies does not actually make the installation of the package
fail. The next time it would show up as a problem would be when loading
the package.

--Brian Diggs
